disclaimer: This pass maps legal pathways and risk. It is not legal advice, a compliance certification, or a prediction of litigation outcomes.
governing_question: Even if Constitutional Capitalism is economically desirable, what can Arkansas actually do under the Arkansas Constitution, the U.S. Constitution, federal law, existing local-government authority, contractual obligations, and protected individual rights?
stance: We do not try to win every argument. We classify authority, risk, and required pathway. Claims die for good legal reasons.

legal_grades.L-B: DEFENSIBLE — Likely lawful with careful design
legal_grades.L-D: HIGH RISK — Likely litigation / narrow path
legal_grades.L-E: NOT VIABLE AS DESIGNED — Conflicts materially with controlling law

constitutional_spine.title: Arkansas constitutional authority spine
constitutional_spine.purpose: One spine every proposal is checked against — prevents repetitive analysis.

nodes.label: Taxing authority
nodes.rule: General Assembly holds primary state taxing power; local taxes require constitutional/statutory authorization; uniformity and classification constraints apply.
nodes.cc_implication: IIT reduction is statutory pathway; school URT is constitutional hardness.

nodes.label: Appropriations
nodes.rule: Public money spent only by appropriation for public purposes; dedicated funds and earmarks bind sequencing.
nodes.cc_implication: Public-income engines cannot spend ahead of lawful appropriation and Replacement Readiness.

nodes.label: Public purpose
nodes.rule: Expenditures and credit uses must serve a public purpose; private benefit is scrutinized (e.g., Pulaski County v. Jacuzzi Bros. line).
nodes.cc_implication: Economic development and equity stakes need direct public return and neutral process — not favoritism.

nodes.label: State debt / bonds
nodes.rule: Amendment 20 generally requires voter approval for bonds pledging state faith/credit/revenues; revenue-bond and authority structures are fact-specific exceptions/designs.
nodes.cc_implication: Large transition financing may need voter ratification — political difficulty ≠ legal impossibility.

nodes.label: Lending of credit (Art. 16 §1)
nodes.rule: Neither State nor municipalities may lend credit for any purpose; using credit for the State's own public purpose is distinct from guaranteeing private debts.
nodes.cc_implication: Guaranteeing private partner debt / suretyship structures are high-risk or not viable as designed.

nodes.label: State investment
nodes.rule: Investment of public funds is constrained by statute, fiduciary rules, and public-purpose doctrine; below-market returns for private benefit invite challenge.
nodes.cc_implication: Pension/development deployment must clear fiduciary + public-purpose tests.

nodes.label: Public corporations / authorities
nodes.rule: Legislature may create authorities and public corporations for defined public purposes with enabling statutes.
nodes.cc_implication: Narrow utility/authority models are clearer than open-ended public businesses.

nodes.label: Local government authority
nodes.rule: Counties/cities/school districts exercise delegated powers; home-rule scope is limited; Dillon-type constraints and state preemption remain material.
nodes.cc_implication: Many 'local pilots' need enabling statutes — not pure local autonomy.

nodes.label: Property taxation
nodes.rule: School URT and related constitutional school-finance structures; local millage classes; debt-service pledges create contractual hardness.
nodes.cc_implication: Full property-tax abolition = amendment + covenant unwind path (4.1 fiscal + 4.2 legal).

nodes.label: Education obligations
nodes.rule: State has constitutional education duty; adequacy/equity litigation history shapes funding redesign.
nodes.cc_implication: Revenue replacement cannot orphan adequacy without legal redesign.

nodes.label: Special / local legislation
nodes.rule: Constitutional limits on special/local acts; classification must be genuine.
nodes.cc_implication: County-only carve-outs need careful classification or general enabling acts.

nodes.label: Equal protection / privileges
nodes.rule: State and federal equal protection; privileges & immunities for nonresidents in some contexts.
nodes.cc_implication: Residency pricing and procurement preferences need rational/bona fide design.

nodes.label: Initiative and referendum
nodes.rule: Amendment 7 pathways; single-subject and signature rules; judicial review; rights floors constrain majority power.
nodes.cc_implication: Structural reforms may require voter ratification; rights floors are not optional.

nodes.label: Constitutional amendments
nodes.rule: Legislatively referred or initiated amendments; distinct from ordinary statutes.
nodes.cc_implication: URT redesign / some democracy reforms live here — transition facts, not automatic failure.

nodes.label: Public funds
nodes.rule: Misapplication / illegal exaction doctrines; dedicated revenues; FOIA/public records overlay.
nodes.cc_implication: COUNTABLE waterfall is also a legal culture: no spending of hoped-for cash.

nodes.label: Governmental immunity (where relevant)
nodes.rule: Immunity is limited and statutory; does not authorize unconstitutional action.
nodes.cc_implication: Digital Due Process and takings claims remain live risk channels.

public_ownership_investment.title: Public ownership & public investment (hardest attack)

questions_and_answers.q: Does Arkansas have authority to own a public enterprise?
questions_and_answers.a: Yes for defined public purposes via enabling statutes/authorities/municipal utilities — not as a general commercial default.
If appropriated for public purpose and structured as the State's own enterprise — not as a gift to private parties.
Yes to guarantees/suretyship of private debts. Art. 16 §1 is a material kill-switch for many PPP guarantee designs.

questions_and_answers.q: Can the state own equity / share upside?
questions_and_answers.a: Defensible with legislation and clear public claim; still L-C until specific structure drafted.

questions_and_answers.q: Can it guarantee private partner debt?
questions_and_answers.a: Generally NOT_LEGALLY_VIABLE AS DESIGNED under lending-of-credit — redesign required.

questions_and_answers.q: Can it subsidize operating losses indefinitely?
questions_and_answers.a: Appropriation + public-purpose possible but politically and legally fragile; looks like private benefit if selective.

questions_and_answers.q: Can a public entity regulate a market it participates in?
questions_and_answers.a: Role Conflict / due process risk — Four Roles test is legally load-bearing, not optional branding.

hostile_case.name: Art. 16 §1 lending-of-credit line (Hays / Turner / AG opinions)
hostile_case.rule: Public bodies may not lend credit; private debt guarantees are classic risk.
hostile_case.why_threatens: CC public-private upside models that rely on state guarantees fail.
hostile_case.distinguishing: Own-purpose enterprise / revenue authority ≠ private suretyship.
hostile_case.disposition: FAILED_AS_DESIGNED for guarantee-heavy models; SURVIVED_WITH_REDESIGN for narrow authorities.

public_ownership_investment.redesign: Prefer function-limited authorities, retained equity/royalty, competitive process, no private debt guarantee, Role Conflict walls.

tax_pathways.title: Tax abolition & replacement pathways (legality, not wisdom)

items.note: Politically hard; legally possible by statute. 4.1 fiscal kill of near-term dual abolition still stands.
Bondholder rights — FAILED AS DESIGNED if ignored.

items.pathway: Local + statutory authorization; voter approval often
items.note: Distinguish fees from taxes; uniformity issues.
Federal program interactions possible; still statute-primary.

local_subsidiarity.title: Local government & subsidiarity
local_subsidiarity.finding: Arkansas local power is delegated and often preemption-sensitive. A pilot needing state permission is not autonomous — it changes the transition map.

local_pilot_legal_ladder.label: Local action now
local_pilot_legal_ladder.examples: Existing zoning, municipal utility ops within current charters

local_pilot_legal_ladder.label: State enabling statute
local_pilot_legal_ladder.examples: New special districts, land banks, regional authorities

local_pilot_legal_ladder.label: Statewide legislation
local_pilot_legal_ladder.examples: Uniform procurement, residency tuition rules, Digital Due Process code

public_purpose_test.title: Public purpose test (legal)
checklist: Is benefit primarily public or private?
How direct is the public return?
Does the state retain contractual/equity interest?
public_purpose_test.note: Connects procurement, ED, PPP, research/IP, capital access, ownership.

procurement.title: Procurement & Arkansas preference
procurement.finding: Blanket Arkansas-first mandates that burden interstate commerce — especially on federally funded buys — are not viable as designed. Narrow tools (small-business, market-participant proprietary purchases, carefully drafted resident preferences off federal funds) can be defensible.

hostile_case.name: Dormant Commerce Clause / discrimination against interstate commerce
hostile_case.why_threatens: In-state preference on competitive interstate markets invites invalidation.
hostile_case.distinguishing: Market-participant doctrine; proprietary functions; federal funding carve-outs compliance.
hostile_case.disposition: CX-P3-03 SURVIVED_WITH_REDESIGN — lawful toolkit, not ideological insistence.

education_residency.title: Education & residency
findings: Resident vs nonresident tuition differentials are an established L-B pathway if domicile is bona fide.
Durational waiting periods for benefits face federal constitutional limits (travel/equal protection).
Residency, not citizenship — locked; immigration rules constrain international structures.
Post-graduation service conditions / recoupment: possible as contractual voluntary programs (L-C/L-D); coercive designs HIGH RISK.
Moving after benefit: contract design + notice; cannot invent peonage.

research_ip.title: Research / IP & public upside
findings: University-created IP today: institutional policies + inventor shares.
Federally funded research: Bayh-Dole and grant conditions dominate.
Arkansas may encourage equity/royalty participation for state-funded work — must not contradict federal title rules.
Public universities holding equity: often authorized with policy firewalls.
Aggressive claims that chill collaboration are policy risk (4.3) more than pure illegality — authority is conditional.

banking_credit_pensions.title: Banking, credit, investment & pension capital
findings: Direct lending / revolving funds / ED authorities: existing toolkit — L-B with statutes.
Guaranteeing private borrowing: Art. 16 §1 — L-E as designed.
Pension deployment for Arkansas development: fiduciary duty constrains 'below-market for vibes' — L-D if forced.
Public deposits / credit enhancement: fact-specific; avoid suretyship.
Public bank project not required by architecture; boundary map preferred.

routes.eminent_domain: Authorized with public use/purpose + just compensation — HIGH process risk if abuse

healthcare_retirement.title: Healthcare & retirement — federal dominance map
healthcare_retirement.note: Status means federal law dominates many fields — not that Arkansas can do nothing. State insurance regulation, public providers, Medicaid administration, and public pensions remain live. Private employer mandates / ERISA space often FEDERAL_CONSTRAINT.

energy_resources.title: Energy, utilities & natural resources
energy_resources.boundary: Mixed state/federal. Municipal utilities and coops have clear lanes; interstate transmission/export and environmental overlays are federal-heavy.

digital_due_process.title: AI, data & Digital Due Process
digital_due_process.core_question: At what point does an AI-assisted system become an exercise of state power requiring procedural protection?
digital_due_process.survives: Arkansas can use AI in many contexts; notice/appeal/human review for consequential eligibility is L-B architecture.
digital_due_process.unresolved: Edge cases on algorithmic discrimination standards, search/seizure analogies, and emerging federal privacy law — Stage 4 legal uncertainty allowed.
flow: Does it determine rights/benefits/sanctions? → state action trigger
Access to record / explanation adequate for challenge

direct_democracy.title: Direct democracy & constitutional change
direct_democracy.finding: Majority cannot strip federal/state constitutional rights floors (CX-P3-02).

speech_pay_to_play.title: Speech / pay-to-play hostility (CX-P3-01)
speech_pay_to_play.finding: Disclosure, recusal, contracting bans for donors, and pay-to-play limits can be L-B if carefully tailored. Content-based speech bans or punishing disfavored speakers are L-E.

hostile_case.name: Citizens United / free-speech campaign finance line (federal)
hostile_case.why_threatens: Overbroad hostility to political speech collapses.
hostile_case.distinguishing: Regulate corruption/access in contracting and official action — not viewpoint punishment.

antitrust_reach.title: State antitrust reach vs federal preemption (CX-M21-02 / OV-34-02 / OV-35-03)
antitrust_reach.finding: Arkansas may have complementary enforcement and state unfair-practice tools; it cannot contradict the Sherman Act or invent immunity for private cartels. Parker state-action immunity is narrow and requires clear articulation + active supervision when private parties are involved.

rights_matrix.title: Rights audit (compact)
rights_matrix.rule: No proposal gets a pass merely because its economic objective is attractive.

collisions.result: Bona fide domicile; limit durational traps
Digital Due Process mandatory for consequential decisions

what_changed_format.what_we_thought: Many CC mechanisms could proceed as ordinary policy choices once economically designed.
what_changed_format.what_law_allows: Statutory IIT pathway; resident tuition differentials; narrow authorities/utilities; Digital Due Process architecture; complementary antitrust; rights-floored direct democracy; public purpose investment with retained claims.
what_changed_format.what_law_conditions: Enabling statutes; public purpose; competitive process; Role Conflict walls; fiduciary rules; federal grant/Medicaid/ERISA envelopes; bona fide domicile.
what_changed_format.what_requires_amendment: Full URT/school constitutional property redesign; some deep democracy/local-power reconstructions.
what_changed_format.what_requires_federal_change: Large private-employer retirement/healthcare mandate space; some interstate energy overlays — federal dominance map, not Arkansas impotence.
what_changed_format.what_failed: Default public ownership; private debt guarantees; blanket Arkansas-first procurement; ignoring bond covenants; speech-punishing pay-to-play; coercive service conditions; consequential AI without process; pure local autonomy fiction.
what_changed_format.what_we_redesigned: Ownership-by-function authorities; procurement toolkit; pay-to-play as anti-corruption; I&R with rights floors; Local Pilot Legal Ladder; voluntary reciprocal education contracts.
what_changed_format.what_remains_legally_uncertain: AI state-action edges (OV-35-05); specific equity/authority statutes not yet drafted; Parker immunity fact patterns; some housing anti-speculation designs.
